text: The AI system has classified the brain MRI as "No Tumour", meaning it did not detect image features that correspond to the three tumour types it was trained on - glioma, meningioma or pituitary tumour [neurasight-system]. It is important to understand that this output is a classification, not a definitive medical diagnosis, and it does not equate to a normal scan [neurasight-system]. The model only recognises four categories; any other abnormality such as infarct, haemorrhage, infection or developmental anomaly may be placed into the "No Tumour" class because the algorithm has no way to express "something else" [nci-cns-pdq-patient]. Likewise, a lack of tumour detection does not guarantee the absence of disease, a single slice does not represent the whole study, and clinical correlation remains essential [nci-cns-pdq-patient]. If the patient has symptoms such as sudden severe headache, new seizures, loss of consciousness, focal weakness, visual change, confusion or persistent vomiting, urgent medical assessment is still required [ninds-brain-tumors]. In such circumstances a clinician may discuss a thorough neurological examination, formal radiological reporting of the complete imaging set, repeat or additional imaging with appropriate sequences, evaluation for non-tumour causes and possible specialist referral [nci-cns-pdq-patient] [ninds-brain-tumors].
